lines.text: I have a little yet to say. Look there, my lords.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: By virtue of that ring, I take my cause

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Out of the gripes of cruel men and give it

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: To a most noble judge, the King my master.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: This is the King’s ring.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: ’Tis no counterfeit.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: ’Tis the right ring, by heaven! I told ye all,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: When we first put this dangerous stone a-rolling,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: ’Twould fall upon ourselves.

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: Do you think, my lords,

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: The King will suffer but the little finger

lines.speaker: NORFOLK
lines.text: Of this man to be vexed?

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: ’Tis now too certain.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: How much more is his life in value with him?

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Would I were fairly out on’t!

lines.speaker: CROMWELL
lines.text: My mind gave me,

lines.speaker: CROMWELL
lines.text: In seeking tales and informations

lines.speaker: CROMWELL
lines.text: Against this man, whose honesty the devil

lines.speaker: CROMWELL
lines.text: And his disciples only envy at,

lines.speaker: CROMWELL
lines.text: Ye blew the fire that burns ye. Now have at ye!
Enter King, frowning on them; takes his seat.

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: Dread sovereign, how much are we bound to heaven

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: In daily thanks, that gave us such a prince,

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: Not only good and wise, but most religious;

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: One that, in all obedience, makes the Church

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: The chief aim of his honour and, to strengthen

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: That holy duty out of dear respect,

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: His royal self in judgement comes to hear

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: The cause betwixt her and this great offender.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You were ever good at sudden commendations,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Bishop of Winchester. But know I come not

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To hear such flattery now, and in my presence

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: They are too thin and bare to hide offences.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To me you cannot reach, you play the spaniel,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And think with wagging of your tongue to win me;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But whatsoe’er thou tak’st me for, I’m sure

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou hast a cruel nature and a bloody.
[_To Cranmer_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Good man, sit down. Now let me see the proudest

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He, that dares most, but wag his finger at thee.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: By all that’s holy, he had better starve

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Than but once think this place becomes thee not.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: May it please your Grace—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: No, sir, it does not please me.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I had thought I had had men of some understanding

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And wisdom of my Council, but I find none.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Was it discretion, lords, to let this man,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This good man—few of you deserve that title—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This honest man, wait like a lousy footboy

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: At chamber door? And one as great as you are?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why, what a shame was this! Did my commission

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Bid ye so far forget yourselves? I gave ye

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Power as he was a councillor to try him,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Not as a groom. There’s some of ye, I see,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: More out of malice than integrity,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Would try him to the utmost, had ye mean,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which ye shall never have while I live.

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: Thus far,

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: My most dread sovereign, may it like your Grace

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: To let my tongue excuse all. What was purposed

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: Concerning his imprisonment was rather,

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: If there be faith in men, meant for his trial

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: And fair purgation to the world than malice,

lines.speaker: CHANCELLOR
lines.text: I’m sure, in me.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Well, well, my lords, respect him.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Take him, and use him well; he’s worthy of it.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I will say thus much for him: if a prince

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: May be beholding to a subject, I

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Am, for his love and service, so to him.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Make me no more ado, but all embrace him.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Be friends, for shame, my lords! My Lord of Canterbury,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I have a suit which you must not deny me:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That is, a fair young maid that yet wants baptism.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You must be godfather and answer for her.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: The greatest monarch now alive may glory

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: In such an honour. How may I deserve it,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: That am a poor and humble subject to you?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Come, come, my lord, you’d spare your spoons. You shall have two noble

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: partners with you: the old Duchess of Norfolk and Lady Marquess Dorset.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Will these please you?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Once more, my Lord of Winchester, I charge you,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Embrace and love this man.

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: With a true heart

lines.speaker: GARDINER
lines.text: And brother-love I do it.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And let heaven

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Witness how dear I hold this confirmation.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Good man, those joyful tears show thy true heart.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The common voice, I see, is verified

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of thee, which says thus: “Do my Lord of Canterbury

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A shrewd turn, and he is your friend for ever.”

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Come, lords, we trifle time away. I long

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To have this young one made a Christian.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As I have made ye one, lords, one remain.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So I grow stronger, you more honour gain.
[_Exeunt._]
Noise and tumult within. Enter Porter and his Man.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: You’ll leave your noise anon, ye rascals. Do you take the court for

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Parish Garden? Ye rude slaves, leave your gaping.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: ONE
lines.text: Good master porter, I belong to th’ larder.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Belong to th’ gallows, and be hanged, ye rogue! Is this a place to roar

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: in? Fetch me a dozen crab-tree staves, and strong ones. These are but

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: switches to ’em. I’ll scratch your heads. You must be seeing

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: christenings? Do you look for ale and cakes here, you rude rascals?

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: Pray, sir, be patient. ’Tis as much impossible—

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: Unless we sweep ’em from the door with cannons—

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: To scatter ’em as ’tis to make ’em sleep

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: On May-day morning, which will never be.

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: We may as well push against Paul’s as stir ’em.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: How got they in, and be hanged?

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: Alas, I know not. How gets the tide in?

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: As much as one sound cudgel of four foot—

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: You see the poor remainder—could distribute,

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: I made no spare, sir.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: You did nothing, sir.

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: I am not Samson, nor Sir Guy, nor Colbrand,

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: To mow ’em down before me; but if I spared any

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: That had a head to hit, either young or old,

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: He or she, cuckold or cuckold-maker,

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: Let me ne’er hope to see a chine again—

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: And that I would not for a cow, God save her!
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: ONE
lines.text: Do you hear, master porter?

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: I shall be with you presently, good master puppy.—

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Keep the door close, sirrah.

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: What would you have me do?

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: What should you do, but knock ’em down by th’ dozens? Is this

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Moorfields to muster in? Or have we some strange Indian with the great

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: tool come to court, the women so besiege us? Bless me, what a fry of

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: fornication is at door! On my Christian conscience, this one

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: christening will beget a thousand; here will be father, godfather, and

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: all together.

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: The spoons will be the bigger, sir. There is a fellow somewhat near the

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: door—he should be a brazier by his face, for, o’ my conscience, twenty

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: of the dog-days now reign in’s nose. All that stand about him are under

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: the line; they need no other penance. That fire-drake did I hit three

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: times on the head, and three times was his nose discharged against me.

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: He stands there, like a mortar-piece, to blow us. There was a

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: haberdasher’s wife of small wit near him that railed upon me till her

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: pinked porringer fell off her head for kindling such a combustion in

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: the state. I missed the meteor once and hit that woman, who cried out

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: “Clubs!” when I might see from far some forty truncheoners draw to her

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: succour, which were the hope o’ th’ Strand, where she was quartered.

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: They fell on; I made good my place; at length they came to th’

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: broomstaff to me; I defied ’em still, when suddenly a file of boys

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: behind ’em, loose shot, delivered such a shower of pebbles that I was

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: fain to draw mine honour in and let ’em win the work. The devil was

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: amongst ’em, I think, surely.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: These are the youths that thunder at a playhouse and fight for bitten

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: apples, that no audience but the tribulation of Tower Hill or the limbs

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: of Limehouse, their dear brothers, are able to endure. I have some of

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: ’em in _Limbo Patrum_, and there they are like to dance these three

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: days, besides the running banquet of two beadles that is to come.
Enter Lord Chamberlain.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Mercy o’ me, what a multitude are here!

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: They grow still too. From all parts they are coming,

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: As if we kept a fair here! Where are these porters,

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: These lazy knaves? You’ve made a fine hand, fellows!

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: There’s a trim rabble let in. Are all these

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Your faithful friends o’ th’ suburbs? We shall have

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Great store of room, no doubt, left for the ladies,

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: When they pass back from the christening.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: An’t please your honour,

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: We are but men; and what so many may do,

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Not being torn a-pieces, we have done.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: An army cannot rule ’em.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: As I live,

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: If the King blame me for’t, I’ll lay ye all

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: By th’ heels, and suddenly, and on your heads

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Clap round fines for neglect. You’re lazy knaves,

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: And here ye lie baiting of bombards, when

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Ye should do service. Hark, the trumpets sound!

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: They’re come already from the christening.

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: Go break among the press, and find a way out

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: To let the troops pass fairly, or I’ll find

lines.speaker: CHAMBERLAIN
lines.text: A Marshalsea shall hold ye play these two months.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Make way there for the Princess!

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: You great fellow,

lines.speaker: PORTER’S MAN
lines.text: Stand close up, or I’ll make your head ache.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: You i’ th’ camlet, get up o’ th’ rail!

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: I’ll peck you o’er the pales else.
[_Exeunt._]

Enter Trumpets, sounding; then two Aldermen, Lord Mayor, Garter, Cranmer, Duke of Norfolk with his marshal’s staff, Duke of Suffolk, two Noblemen bearing great standing bowls for the christening gifts; then four Noblemen bearing a canopy, under which the Duchess of Norfolk, godmother, bearing the child richly habited in a mantle, etc., train borne by a Lady; then follows the Marchioness Dorset, the other godmother, and Ladies. The troop pass once about the stage, and Garter speaks.

lines.speaker: GARTER
lines.text: Heaven, from thy endless goodness, send prosperous life, long and ever

lines.speaker: GARTER
lines.text: happy, to the high and mighty Princess of England, Elizabeth.
Flourish. Enter King and Guard.
[_Kneeling_.]

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And to your royal Grace and the good Queen,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: My noble partners and myself thus pray

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: All comfort, joy, in this most gracious lady

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Heaven ever laid up to make parents happy

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: May hourly fall upon ye!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thank you, good lord Archbishop.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What is her name?

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Elizabeth.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Stand up, lord.
[_The King kisses the child._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With this kiss take my blessing: God protect thee,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Into whose hand I give thy life.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Amen.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My noble gossips, you’ve have been too prodigal.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I thank ye heartily; so shall this lady,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When she has so much English.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Let me speak, sir,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: For heaven now bids me; and the words I utter

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Let none think flattery, for they’ll find ’em truth.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: This royal infant—heaven still move about her!—

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Though in her cradle, yet now promises

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Upon this land a thousand thousand blessings,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Which time shall bring to ripeness. She shall be—

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: But few now living can behold that goodness—

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: A pattern to all princes living with her

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And all that shall succeed. Saba was never

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: More covetous of wisdom and fair virtue

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Than this pure soul shall be. All princely graces

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: That mould up such a mighty piece as this is,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: With all the virtues that attend the good,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Shall still be doubled on her. Truth shall nurse her;

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Holy and heavenly thoughts still counsel her.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: She shall be loved and feared. Her own shall bless her;

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Her foes shake like a field of beaten corn,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And hang their heads with sorrow. Good grows with her.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: In her days every man shall eat in safety

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Under his own vine what he plants, and sing

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: The merry songs of peace to all his neighbours.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: God shall be truly known, and those about her

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: From her shall read the perfect ways of honour

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And by those claim their greatness, not by blood.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Nor shall this peace sleep with her; but as when

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: The bird of wonder dies, the maiden phoenix,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Her ashes new create another heir

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: As great in admiration as herself,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: So shall she leave her blessedness to one,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: When heaven shall call her from this cloud of darkness,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Who from the sacred ashes of her honour

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Shall star-like rise as great in fame as she was

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And so stand fixed. Peace, plenty, love, truth, terror,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: That were the servants to this chosen infant,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Shall then be his, and like a vine grow to him.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Wherever the bright sun of heaven shall shine,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: His honour and the greatness of his name

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Shall be, and make new nations. He shall flourish,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And, like a mountain cedar, reach his branches

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: To all the plains about him. Our children’s children

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Shall see this and bless heaven.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou speakest wonders.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: She shall be to the happiness of England

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: An aged princess; many days shall see her,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And yet no day without a deed to crown it.

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: Would I had known no more! But she must die,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: She must, the saints must have her; yet a virgin,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: A most unspotted lily, shall she pass to the ground,

lines.speaker: CRANMER
lines.text: And all the world shall mourn her.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O lord Archbishop,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou hast made me now a man. Never before

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This happy child did I get anything.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This oracle of comfort has so pleased me

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That when I am in heaven I shall desire

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To see what this child does and praise my Maker.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I thank ye all. To you, my good Lord Mayor,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And you, good brethren, I am much beholding.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I have received much honour by your presence,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And ye shall find me thankful. Lead the way, lords.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ye must all see the Queen, and she must thank ye;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: She will be sick else. This day, no man think

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: ’Has business at his house, for all shall stay.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This little one shall make it holiday.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Epilogue
Enter Epilogue.

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: ’Tis ten to one this play can never please

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: All that are here. Some come to take their ease,

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: And sleep an act or two—but those, we fear,

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: We’ve frighted with our trumpets; so, ’tis clear,

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: They’ll say ’tis naught—others, to hear the city

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: Abused extremely and to cry “That’s witty!”—

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: Which we have not done neither—that I fear

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: All the expected good we’re like to hear

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: For this play at this time is only in

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: The merciful construction of good women,

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: For such a one we showed ’em. If they smile

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: And say ’twill do, I know within a while

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: All the best men are ours; for ’tis ill hap

lines.speaker: EPILOGUE
lines.text: If they hold when their ladies bid ’em clap.
[_Exit._]
